propositions.name: astronomic_universe_of_masses
propositions.quote: The astronomic universe is formed of masses, very great, no doubt, but separated by intervals so immense that they appear to us only as material points.
propositions.statement: The astronomic universe is formed of masses separated by intervals so immense that they appear to us only as material points.

propositions.name: inverse_square_sole_force
propositions.quote: These points attract each other inversely as the square of the distance, and this attraction is the sole force which influences their movements.
propositions.statement: The material points of the astronomic universe attract each other inversely as the square of the distance, and this attraction is the sole force which influences their movements.

propositions.name: matter_resembles_astronomic_spectacle
propositions.quote: There also we should see material points, separated from one another by intervals, enormous in comparison with their dimensions, and describing orbits according to regular laws.
propositions.statement: If our senses were keen enough to show us the details of the bodies the physicist studies, we should see material points separated by intervals enormous in comparison with their dimensions, describing orbits according to regular laws.

propositions.name: infinitesimal_stars_are_atoms
propositions.quote: These infinitesimal stars are the atoms. Like the stars proper, they attract or repel each other,
propositions.statement: The infinitesimal stars found among the details of bodies are the atoms, and like the stars proper they attract or repel each other.

propositions.name: atoms_attract_repel_by_distance
propositions.quote: and this attraction or this repulsion, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.
propositions.statement: The attraction or repulsion between atoms, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.

propositions.name: force_law_power_of_distance
propositions.quote: The law according to which this force varies as function of the distance is perhaps not the law of Newton, but it is an analogous law; in place of the exponent −2, we have probably a different exponent
propositions.statement: The law according to which the force between atoms varies as a function of the distance is an analogous law to that of Newton, with probably a different exponent in place of the exponent −2.

propositions.name: exponent_change_yields_diversity
propositions.quote: it is from this change of exponent that arises all the diversity of physical phenomena, the variety of qualities and of sensations, all the world, colored and sonorous, which surrounds us
propositions.statement: It is from the change of exponent that arises all the diversity of physical phenomena, the variety of qualities and of sensations, all the world, colored and sonorous, which surrounds us.

propositions.name: capillarity_case_of_attraction
propositions.quote: he regards it only as a particular case of attraction, or, as he says, of universal gravitation, and no one is astonished to find it in the middle of one of the five volumes
propositions.statement: Capillarity is only a particular case of attraction, or of universal gravitation.

propositions.name: ether_atoms_sixth_power_attraction
propositions.quote: the atoms of ether attract each other in the inverse ratio of the sixth power of the distance; and Maxwell himself, does he not say somewhere that
propositions.statement: The atoms of ether attract each other in the inverse ratio of the sixth power of the distance.

propositions.name: gas_atoms_fifth_power_repulsion
propositions.quote: the atoms of gases repel each other in the inverse ratio of the fifth power of the distance?
propositions.statement: The atoms of gases repel each other in the inverse ratio of the fifth power of the distance.

propositions.name: fourier_atoms_transmit_heat
propositions.quote: in it are indeed atoms acting at a distance one upon the other; they mutually transmit heat, but they do not attract, they never budge.
propositions.statement: In Fourier's theory, atoms act at a distance one upon the other and mutually transmit heat, but they do not attract and they never budge.

propositions.name: matter_has_ultimate_elements
propositions.quote: they know that one will attain the ultimate elements of things only by patiently disentangling the complicated skein that our senses give us
propositions.statement: One will attain the ultimate elements of things only by patiently disentangling the complicated skein that our senses give us.

propositions.name: law_as_differential_equation
propositions.quote: For us a law is something quite different; it is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow; in a word, it is a differential equation.
propositions.statement: For us a law is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow, that is, a differential equation.

propositions.name: conservation_of_energy_principle
propositions.quote: The principle of the conservation of energy, or Mayer's principle, is certainly the most important, but it is not the only one
propositions.statement: The principle of the conservation of energy, or Mayer's principle, is certainly the most important of the general principles.

propositions.name: carnot_degradation_of_energy
propositions.quote: Carnot's principle, or the principle of the degradation of energy.
propositions.statement: Carnot's principle is the principle of the degradation of energy.

propositions.name: newtons_principle_action_reaction
propositions.quote: Newton's principle, or the principle of the equality of action and reaction.
propositions.statement: Newton's principle is the principle of the equality of action and reaction.

propositions.name: principle_of_relativity
propositions.quote: The principle of relativity, according to which the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation
propositions.statement: The principle of relativity holds that the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation.

propositions.name: no_detection_of_uniform_motion
propositions.quote: so that we have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in such a motion.
propositions.statement: We have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in a uniform motion of translation.

propositions.name: conservation_of_mass
propositions.quote: The principle of the conservation of mass, or Lavoisier's principle.
propositions.statement: The principle of the conservation of mass is Lavoisier's principle.

propositions.name: principle_of_least_action
propositions.quote: I will add the principle of least action. The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.
propositions.statement: There is a principle of least action, and the application of these general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.

propositions.name: principles_sufficient_for_knowledge
propositions.quote: The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.
propositions.statement: The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.

propositions.name: maxwell_electromagnetic_theory_of_light
propositions.quote: The most remarkable example of this new mathematical physics is, beyond question, Maxwell's electromagnetic theory of light.
propositions.statement: The most remarkable example of the new mathematical physics is Maxwell's electromagnetic theory of light.

propositions.name: ether_transmits_optical_electrical
propositions.quote: we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations
propositions.statement: The ether is a medium that transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations.

propositions.name: ether_has_unknown_molecules
propositions.quote: We know nothing as to what the ether is, how its molecules are disposed, whether they attract or repel each other; but we know that this medium transmits
propositions.statement: The ether has molecules that are disposed in some way and that may attract or repel each other, though we know nothing as to what the ether is or how they are disposed.

propositions.name: transmission_conforms_to_mechanics
propositions.quote: we know that this transmission must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics, and that suffices us for the establishment of the equations of the electromagnetic field.
propositions.statement: The transmission of the optical and electrical perturbations by the ether must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics.

propositions.name: principles_derive_certainty_from_generality
propositions.quote: These principles are results of experiments boldly generalized; but they seem to derive from their very generality a high degree of certainty.
propositions.statement: These principles are results of experiments boldly generalized, and they seem to derive from their very generality a high degree of certainty.

propositions.name: central_forces_entail_principles
propositions.quote: The hypothesis of central forces contained all the principles; it involved them as necessary consequences; it involved both the conservation of energy and that of masses, and the equality of action and reaction, and the law of least action
propositions.statement: The hypothesis of central forces contained all the principles and involved them as necessary consequences, including the conservation of energy, the conservation of masses, the equality of action and reaction, and the law of least action.

propositions.name: universe_is_a_machine
propositions.quote: The universe is also a machine, much more complicated than all those of industry, of which almost all the parts are profoundly hidden from us
propositions.statement: The universe is a machine, much more complicated than all those of industry, of which almost all the parts are profoundly hidden from us.

propositions.name: conservation_of_energy_true_conclusions
propositions.quote: we are able, by the aid of this principle, to draw conclusions which remain true whatever may be the details of the invisible mechanism which animates them.
propositions.statement: By the aid of the principle of the conservation of energy, we are able to draw conclusions about the universe which remain true whatever may be the details of the invisible mechanism which animates the parts we cannot see.
